original_image: Recognizable simple blue shipwreck silhouette: wide low hull with a sloped right tip, squat cabin on the right, and leaning mast/crossbar left of center.
Large flat blue surfaces and sharp geometric edges dominate. The hull front is dark navy blue while upward surfaces are brighter cyan blue; the mast reads as a thin rectangular strip.
No visible broken plank structure, rope, growth, barnacles or surrounding stones. Material separation is mainly broad blue value changes.
fixed_target: Retains the wide low blue hull, right cabin and left-of-center mast/crossbar identity, but makes the components rounded and substantially more physically built.
Hull consists visually of chunky horizontal blue timber courses with uneven edges, warm exposed wood at cuts, a dark broken opening at left, and visible seams that follow the timber construction.

Mast and crossbar become rounded timber, wrapped at their junction with thick cream rope. Long green seaweed drapes from the crossbar and grows against the hull; pale barnacles and rounded stones cluster near the lower corners.
Broad turquoise face gradients, soft darker undersides and warm yellow-gold top/right edge light give volume. Rounded bevels receive thick highlights rather than uniform razor outlines.

The image has more surface and silhouette detail than the quiet original. Its decorative richness is a visible style/design opportunity; this observation is not a claim that every target detail is mandatory or technically admissible.
global_style: Reference plant uses saturated green broad facets over an ochre golden pot, with large readable planes and softened edge transitions.
Bright warm yellow rim highlights and deeper amber recesses create soft dimensional separation. Facets remain legible rather than being smoothed into a glossy continuous surface.
The reference feels compact, sculpted and warm; its material hierarchy is simple, with a few large highlight/shadow regions and little fine texture.
native_isolation_view: The untouched native collection visually reproduces the same sparse blue hull/cabin/mast/crossbar design as the supplied original image at the saved scene camera.
Small bevels are visible on mast/crossbar/cabin edges, while the hull remains a large planar angular front and shallow top strip. Broad blue gradients do not create separate timber structure.
comparison: Largest visible gaps are built timber volume and rounded silhouettes, structural surface breaks, intentional secondary forms, and warm soft lighting/material response.
The source silhouette is a useful identity basis. Existing mesh count, depth and flat shading are observations, not inferred aesthetic locks.
No future camera, interface, footprint, ground contact or size limits are inferred from the target pixels. The coordinator must freeze actual technical limits separately.
